title: Does the model fit the free tier?

blocks.text: A team at a gas network wants to try commercial solvers on their free tiers before asking for quotes, and needs to know which of its models each free tier accepts. Free tiers cap model size in different ways: some cap variables and constraints separately, some cap their sum, and some have tighter caps when the model has quadratic terms.

A tier is described as `{"linear": caps, "quadratic": caps}`, where `caps` is a tuple `(max_vars, max_rows, max_sum)`, and any of the three may be `None`, meaning that count is not capped. A model fits when its variables are at most `max_vars`, its rows at most `max_rows`, and variables plus rows at most `max_sum`, using the `"quadratic"` caps when the model has quadratic terms and the `"linear"` caps otherwise.
Write `fits(n_vars, n_rows, quadratic, tier)` in `tiers.py`. About five lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from tiers import fits

# A tier caps (variables, rows, variables + rows) per kind of model; None is no cap.
tier = {"linear": (1500, 1000, 2200), "quadratic": (300, 1000, None)}
print("1200 vars, 800 rows, linear:", fits(1200, 800, False, tier))
print("1300 vars, 950 rows, linear:", fits(1300, 950, False, tier))
print("250 vars, 900 rows, quadratic:", fits(250, 900, True, tier))
print("400 vars, 900 rows, quadratic:", fits(400, 900, True, tier))

cases.says: a linear model under every cap fits, and one over the variable cap does not
a count exactly at its cap still fits
a cap on variables plus rows refuses a model whose two counts are each modest but together too many
a model with quadratic terms is checked against the quadratic caps, not the linear ones
a cap given as None does not limit that count
